found_values.value: 200 ms. No source names a deadline for this case itself: docs/Safety.md:51-54 lists 'The panel is healthy and the coprocessor misbehaves' as covered by no hardware. The tree bounds every stop path by the coprocessor's 200 ms link failsafe: LINK_DEV_SILENCE_MS 200u, 'the processor holding the outputs is the more suspicious of the two' (shared/link/include/link_dev.h:29-31). The specification and the monostable page give the deadline as 200 ms, 'no slower than the coprocessor's 200 ms link failsafe' (IOBoard.md:186; Monostable.md:28 and :115-116 at 23c82ca). The watchdog is the only stop path for a frozen coprocessor beside a beating panel, so the same 200 ms applies to it. A deadline read from the tree, not an owner figure

found_values.value: 900 ms for one main-loop pass with a host that stops reading; no bound with a host that keeps accepting data more slowly than it is written. A pass holds at most one flash window: a 4 kB sector erase (W25Q16JV packaged maximum 400 ms) or a page program (3 ms), never both (firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:1049-1087; the reclaim erase runs only on an idle pass). A printf follows the window in the same pass (main.c:1051-1086), and can_report follows at main.c:1089. pico-sdk 2.3.0 and 2.3.1 stdio_usb_out_chars (byte-identical, stdio_usb.c:102-132) waits while the host takes nothing until PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US has passed since the last accepted write; the default is 500,000 us (stdio_usb.h:31-33) and nothing under firmware/ overrides it. 400 ms + 500 ms = 900 ms. Each accepted write restarts the 500 ms, so a slow host sets no bound. The boot pass erases up to OUT_STORE_SECTORS = 2 sectors (out_store.h:122; main.c:937-942), 800 ms plus prints, if the watchdog is already running then. The 400 ms and 3 ms are packaged-part figures; the die's are not known

Table 597 gives the crystal the XOSC is specified with (ABM8-272-T3): CL 10 pF, ESR (R1) 50 Ohm max, drive level 10 uW typical and 200 uW max. The hardware design guide: 'We've opted for a device with a maximum of 50 Ohm, as we've found that this, along with a 1 kOhm series resistor (R2), is a good value to prevent the crystal being over-driven'; the load is two 15 pF capacitors (7.5 pF) plus an assumed 3 pF parasitic, 10.5 pF, 'close enough to the target of 10 pF'. report.value: Yes: a 1 kOhm resistor in series between the BOOT contact and QSPI_SS (QFN-80 pin 75). The hardware design guide wires the USB_BOOT button to QSPI_SS through R6, 1 kOhm: 'It is important to include resistor R6, as this allows the QSPI_SS pin to safely over-drive the applied pull-down when the RP2350 starts booting'. For the RP2354 it removes the external flash and keeps 'the USB_BOOT switch connected to QSPI_SS'. Section 14.3: CSn driven low at reset 'harmlessly selects the internal flash die but does not issue commands to it'. On the IO board the BOOT button and the bench relay contact across it both reach QSPI_SS through that one resistor. The guide's optional 10 kOhm pull-up on QSPI_SS (R1, DNF) was found unnecessary 'with this particular flash device', its external flash; for the in-package W25Q16JVWI this is not stated

report.value: By source reading, target/rp2350.cfg reaches the RP2354B and programs its in-package flash; not tested on an RP2354B. The config attaches to the RP2350 die over SWD (CPUTAPID 0x00040927, Cortex-M33 cores at AP 0x2000 and 0x4000, USE_CORE { cm0 cm1 } by default) and defines 'flash bank $_FLASHNAME rp2xxx 0x10000000 $_FLASHSIZE' with FLASHSIZE 0 meaning detect. rp2xxx.c erases and programs through the bootrom's connect_internal_flash, flash_range_erase and flash_range_program, which drive QSPI chip select 0; section 14.3 connects that chip select to the in-package W25Q16JVWI. Size detection reads the JEDEC ID and falls back to SFDP; spi.c:132-133 lists 'win w25q16jv' 0x1540ef and 0x1570ef at 2 MB. Whether the die returns EF 40 15 is not stated in a public document; SFDP or FLASHSIZE 0x200000 covers either case. The bench's OpenOCD 0.12.0+dev snapshot of 2026-02-16 (testbench/README.md:462) postdates the rp2xxx.c changes of 2025-06-29 and rp2350.cfg's change of 2026-02-15, but not rp2350.cfg's latest commit a2c6d1522d of 2026-09-06 ('Use -tap instead of -chain-position'). Erratum E4 matters only for RISC-V SBA, which rp2350.cfg does not select by default

report.value: The RP2350 watchdog is off at reset (CTRL.ENABLE 0), counts down in microseconds from LOAD, maximum 0xffffff, 'approximately 16 seconds' (section 12.9). The image sets no timeout (V4). Stop deadline found (V1): 200 ms. Longest legitimate stall found (V2): 900 ms for one pass, a 400 ms packaged-part sector erase plus a USB printf blocked up to 500,000 us; no bound while a host accepts data more slowly than it is written; up to 800 ms of boot-time erases if the watchdog runs before them. No timeout satisfies both: 900 ms > 200 ms, and the 400 ms erase alone exceeds 200 ms. The silicon's range is not the limit, so this is a conflict of the specification and the firmware, reported to the owner and to P5. It holds while the output binding stays in the in-package flash (Q8) and the console print can block for PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US
